cells.tense: Right now you're at the bench, and the bench is where you know what to attend to.
cells.act: ask how it feels to them and stay with the answer
cells.ask: Take a conversation you'd usually handle by doing something for the person, and ask how it truly feels to them. Stay with the answer without fixing anything yet.
cells.core:
You know what to attend to here. The task in your hands gets your whole weight, and the ones close to you feel that: not a rush of concern, not fussing, just the steady attention of someone who stays. That attention is what keeps the connections whole while the work gets done.

That steadiness is the balance. The next thing it can feed is the part that feels with people, not only the part that holds them. So take a conversation you'd normally handle by doing something for the person involved, and ask how it truly feels to them. Then stay with the answer. You don't have to fix it or carry it. You just have to stay in it long enough to hear where they are. The fixing can wait; the hearing is the point.
cells.sheetLine: Your attention is the thing that steadies what's around you.
cells.place: where you know what to attend to before you can say why

cells.tense: You're already braced for how this will go, and the bracing has its hands on the work.
cells.act: judge the hurt fairly after it has finished
cells.ask: Once your next argument is over, weigh it fairly. Not who started it — what it cost each of you. Give both sides their due, then let it rest.
cells.core:
You keep arriving at the moment before it does, and the bracing is steering. You reach for the bend before the road shows one. You tighten what you're building so it can't be touched. The strength is real; it's just running past the present, and the ones near you can feel it as force rather than steadiness.

Fair judgment is what pulls it back into true. Once your next argument is over, weigh it fairly — not who started it, but what it cost each of you, honestly. Give both sides their due, then let it rest. You'll feel the moment the weighing stops being fair and turns into a verdict. That's when to stop. You're allowed to do this after it's finished instead of before.
cells.sheetLine: You're bracing, and the bracing has its hands on the work.

cells.tense: You're still standing at a door that closed, and your hands are on it.
cells.act: release what is done and keep what is not
cells.ask: Let one finished task sit untouched for a full day, then move to a task that isn't finished. Nothing needs improving in between, and nobody needs a call; when the day is up, your hands can go where they're needed.
cells.core:
Something in you is still at a door that has already closed. You showed up, you did the work, and now the work is done and you're still holding it, waiting for a sign you'll recognise. The strength that used to be in your hands sits on a door that won't move. You know what matters here. You just haven't turned from the closed thing toward the open one.

Letting go is what returns it, and it doesn't need a feeling to go with it. Let one finished task sit untouched for a full day, then move to a task that isn't finished. You'll know it by how your hands want to stay. Let the finished thing be finished. The strength comes back when there's somewhere for it to go.
cells.sheetLine: You're standing at a door that has already closed.
cells.place: where you know what to attend to before you can say why

cells.tense: You're deciding what matters before anyone asks, and you wouldn't call it deciding.
cells.act: start something for the spark of starting
cells.ask: Begin a fresh project this week without a plan, an outcome, or anyone told. A few minutes count. Let the beginning belong to you.
cells.core:
You decide what matters before anyone asks, and when it's named you'd say the room was already going that way. In a group you quietly set what gets attended to, then stand back and call it the consensus. The steering is yours. That's not a flaw in how you work; it's the strongest part of it, running outside your own account.

Claiming the start itself is what returns it. Begin a fresh project this week without a plan, an outcome, or anyone told. A few minutes count. You'll feel the old pull to make it useful, or to hand it to someone else so it's theirs. Let the beginning belong to you. You can decide what comes next once it exists.
